idiom_name: type-tagged node objects with a children accessor table
implementation_notes: JavaScript trees are plain objects distinguished by a type tag ({ type: "BinaryExpression", left, right, operator }); the normalized child collection is an accessor - either a children array on each node or, as the ESTree ecosystem does, a per-type table naming the properties that hold children, so one generic visitor works over every node kind. Classes are optional and add little here; the tag is the discriminator and the accessor is the traversal contract. Keep node payload (operator, value, range) out of the accessor list so passes never walk it.
pitfalls: Deriving children from Object.values walks token, range and location fields too and can recurse into non-node data; keep the per-type accessor table authoritative.
Type tags are strings: a typo produces a node no visitor knows, and the accessor silently returns no children, hiding the whole subtree - validate tags when nodes are built.
Object graphs are mutable and shareable, so two parents can own the same child object; rewrites must decide between copying and in-place mutation to avoid aliasing bugs.
